L1945@P54: Opinion on the Financial Statements
L1946@P54: We have audited the accompanying consolidated balance sheets of HEICO Corporation and
L1947@P54: subsidiaries (the "Company") as of October 31, 2024 and 2023, the related consolidated
L1948@P54: statements of operations, comprehensive income, shareholders' equity, and cash flows, for each
L1949@P54: of the three years in the period ended October 31, 2024, and the related notes and the schedule
L1950@P54: listed in the Index at Item 15 (collectively referred to as the "financial statements"). In our
L1951@P54: opinion, the financial statements present fairly, in all material respects, the financial position of
L1952@P54: the Company as of October 31, 2024 and 2023, and the results of its operations and its cash
L1953@P54: flows for each of the three years in the period ended October 31, 2024, in conformity with
L1954@P54: accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America.
L1955@P54: We have also audited, in accordance with the standards of the Public Company Accounting
L1956@P54: Oversight Board (United States) (PCAOB), the Company's internal control over financial
L1957@P54: reporting as of October 31, 2024, based on criteria established in Internal Control - Integrated
L1958@P54: Framework (2013) issued by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway
L1959@P54: Commission and our report dated December 19, 2024, expressed an unqualified opinion on the
L1960@P54: Company's internal control over financial reporting.
L1961@P54: Basis for Opinion
L1962@P54: These financial statements are the responsibility of the Company's management. Our
L1963@P54: responsibility is to express an opinion on the Company's financial statements based on our
L1964@P54: audits. We are a public accounting firm registered with the PCAOB and are required to be
L1965@P54: independent with respect to the Company in accordance with the U.S. federal securities laws and
L1966@P54: the applicable rules and regulations of the Securities and Exchange Commission and the
L1967@P54: PCAOB.
L1968@P54: We conducted our audits in accordance with the standards of the PCAOB. Those standards
L1969@P54: require that we plan and perform the audit to obtain reasonable assurance about whether the
L1970@P54: financial statements are free of material misstatement, whether due to error or fraud. Our audits
L1971@P54: included performing procedures to assess the risks of material misstatement of the financial
L1972@P54: statements, whether due to error or fraud, and performing procedures that respond to those risks.
L1973@P54: Such procedures included examining, on a test basis, evidence regarding the amounts and
L1974@P54: disclosures in the financial statements. Our audits also included evaluating the accounting
L1975@P54: principles used and significant estimates made by management, as well as evaluating the overall
L1976@P54: presentation of the financial statements. We believe that our audits provide a reasonable basis
L1977@P54: for our opinion.

L1979@P54-55: 52Critical Audit Matter
L1980@P55: The critical audit matter communicated below is a matter arising from the current-period audit of
L1981@P55: the financial statements that was communicated or required to be communicated to the Finance/
L1982@P55: Audit committee and that (1) relates to accounts or disclosures that are material to the financial
L1983@P55: statements and (2) involved our especially challenging, subjective, or complex judgments. The
L1984@P55: communication of critical audit matters does not alter in any way our opinion on the financial
L1985@P55: statements, taken as a whole, and we are not, by communicating the critical audit matter below,
L1986@P55: providing a separate opinion on the critical audit matter or on the accounts or disclosures to
L1987@P55: which it relates.
L1988@P55: Inventories, net - Flight Support Group - Refer to Notes 1 and 3 to the financial statements
L1989@P55: Critical Audit Matter Description
L1990@P55: Inventory is stated at the lower of cost or net realizable value. The Company periodically
L1991@P55: evaluates the carrying value of inventory, which requires management to make significant
L1992@P55: estimates and assumptions related to sales patterns and expected future demand in order to
L1993@P55: estimate the amount necessary to write down any slow moving or obsolete inventory. Changes
L1994@P55: in the assumptions related to future demand and sales patterns could have a significant impact on
L1995@P55: the valuation of finished goods inventory for certain of the Company’s distribution and
L1996@P55: aftermarket parts business units in the Flight Support Group operating segment.
L1997@P55: Given the magnitude of the inventory balances at these business units, coupled with the
L1998@P55: judgments necessary to project sales patterns and expected future demand within these business
L1999@P55: units, auditing such estimates required a high degree of auditor judgment and an increased extent
L2000@P55: of effort when performing audit procedures and evaluating the results of those procedures.
L2001@P55: How the Critical Audit Matter Was Addressed in the Audit
L2002@P55: Our audit procedures related to the expected future demand and sales patterns used by
L2003@P55: management to estimate the valuation reserve on inventory included the following, among
L2004@P55: others:
L2005@P55: • We tested the effectiveness of controls, including those related to evaluating the
L2006@P55: reasonableness of expected future demand and sales patterns.
L2007@P55: • We evaluated the reasonableness of management’s assumptions of future demand and
L2008@P55: sales patterns by performing the following:
L2009@P55: ◦ Utilized historical inventory usage data to analyze the relationship between the
L2010@P55: inventory valuation reserve calculated, the inventory on hand, and the sales trends
L2011@P55: over time.
L2012@P55: Index
L2013@P55-56: 53◦ Compared management’s assumptions to available external market data for
L2014@P56: certain inventory items.
L2015@P56: • We evaluated the accuracy and completeness of the valuation reserve by developing an
L2016@P56: expectation of the reserve balance at the business unit level and comparing it to the
L2017@P56: recorded balance.
L2018@P56: • We tested changes in the inventory valuation reserve and evaluated whether such changes
L2019@P56: were the result of the sale or write off of inventory parts or the result of changes in the
L2020@P56: significant assumptions used to develop the valuation reserve.

L1989@P55: Critical Audit Matter Description
L1990@P55: Inventory is stated at the lower of cost or net realizable value. The Company periodically
L1991@P55: evaluates the carrying value of inventory, which requires management to make significant
L1992@P55: estimates and assumptions related to sales patterns and expected future demand in order to
L1993@P55: estimate the amount necessary to write down any slow moving or obsolete inventory. Changes
L1994@P55: in the assumptions related to future demand and sales patterns could have a significant impact on
L1995@P55: the valuation of finished goods inventory for certain of the Company’s distribution and
L1996@P55: aftermarket parts business units in the Flight Support Group operating segment.
L1997@P55: Given the magnitude of the inventory balances at these business units, coupled with the
L1998@P55: judgments necessary to project sales patterns and expected future demand within these business
L1999@P55: units, auditing such estimates required a high degree of auditor judgment and an increased extent
L2000@P55: of effort when performing audit procedures and evaluating the results of those procedures.
L2001@P55: How the Critical Audit Matter Was Addressed in the Audit
L2002@P55: Our audit procedures related to the expected future demand and sales patterns used by
L2003@P55: management to estimate the valuation reserve on inventory included the following, among
L2004@P55: others:
L2005@P55: • We tested the effectiveness of controls, including those related to evaluating the
L2006@P55: reasonableness of expected future demand and sales patterns.
L2007@P55: • We evaluated the reasonableness of management’s assumptions of future demand and
L2008@P55: sales patterns by performing the following:
L2009@P55: ◦ Utilized historical inventory usage data to analyze the relationship between the
L2010@P55: inventory valuation reserve calculated, the inventory on hand, and the sales trends
L2011@P55: over time.
